subject: English
question_text: "Websites have become most popular destination of the modem world." Do you support the idea? Why or why not? Explain in 2/3 sentences. First Paper  Questions
guide_solution: Yes, I support the idea. Social websites like Face book, Google or twitter have become very popular at present. They are easy and simple to use. They are also cost free. So, people of all ages can use them. They have made the way to the user to be introduced to the whole world. So, the number of users of these networks is increasing day by day.
source: SSC English 1st Paper Test Paper 95 — Cantonment English School, Chittagong

subject: English
question_text: Summarize the above mentioned passage in around
guide_solution: Summary The social networks have opened the way to the users to be known to the whole world. They are very simple and easy to use. They are cost free. They can easily interconnect the uses of the whole world. So people of all ages are using these websites. They can share their interest and activities. They can present themselves before the entire world of presenting their personal profiles by uploading pictures and multimedia contents. Because of all these facilities social medias have become more popular and the number of user is increasing day by day.  অনুবাদ(Passage No. 2) : See Bindubasini Govt. Boys' High School, Tangail. Sl. subject: English
question_text: Read the passage carefully and complete the table below
stimulus: with information from the passage. 1×5=5 Charles Babbage was an English mathematician. He was a mechanical engineer who is best known for originating the concept of computer. He was born on 26 December, 1791 in London. He entered Trinity College on October, 1810. He was transferred to Peter house, Cambridge. He was the top mathematician there. He received an honours degree without examination in 1814. He was elected a fellow of the Royal Society in 1816. From 1828 to 1839 Babbage was Lucasian professor of mathematics at Cambridge University. Babbage is famous for inventing the first mechanical computer in 1822 that eventually led to today's computer.
